transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood Product), Maya Chen (Atlas ML Eng), Ethan Rodriguez (Atlas Eng Mgr), Priya Suresh (Atlas CTO)

Summary:
- Weekly POC check-in to review prefix/KV cache hit rates and discuss prompt reuse strategy and tuning steps.
- Agreed next steps: send updated caching configs, run benchmark, enable telemetry, follow-up next week.

Topics:
- Current cache hit rates (prefix vs KV)
- Prompt normalization and reuse patterns
- TTL and eviction policy tradeoffs
- Benchmark plan and metrics to capture

Notes / Links:
- Referenced doc: caching-configs-v2 (shared drive link)
- Benchmark sheet: atlas-poc-benchmarks.xlsx (customer spreadsheet link)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Okay, uh, thanks everyone for joining the weekly caching sync, we're at 10, thanks for being on time. Quick roll call -- Jordan Lee from Redwood, Priya on the SE side, Samir joining for product.
[00:12] Maya: Hey, hi, Maya here. Ethan and Priya Suresh on as well.
[00:18] Jordan: Cool, quick agenda, review last week's numbers, talk tuning, then plan benchmarks, ok?
[00:26] Priya (SE): Yep, I have the staging metrics open, i'll pull the hit rate numbers in a sec.
[00:33] Priya (Atlas): Great, we're most interested in seeing reductions in p99 latency and token cost.
[00:38] Jordan: Totally. Alright Priya, staging numbers?
[00:42] Priya (SE): So rough numbers: prefix cache hit rate is around 34% across the dataset, KV cache hit rate is showing 18% in staging. There's some overlap, so effective combined hit is ~43%. These are over last 48 hours, traffic slice is the 1% pilot.
[01:02] Maya: Hmm, 18% KV seems lower than we expected, our baseline local test was closer to 30. Could this be due to prompt formatting differences?
[01:11] Priya (SE): Yeah, that's likely. We saw a lot of small variations — trailing spaces, differences in user metadata fields. The prefix caching is catching reused system prompts but KV is more fragile to token-level differences.
[01:26] Samir: Quick clarifying q: when you say prefix cache are you normalizing system messages only or also user instructions?
[01:31] Priya (SE): Right now we normalize system and instruction templates but not user-specific variables. We did implement basic whitespace collapse but not canonicalization of temporal tokens like dates.
[01:41] Ethan: On our side we have some dynamic placeholders in prompts that change per user, that likely busts the KV. We can try moving those to function args rather than inline in prompt.
[01:51] Priya (Atlas): Yeah, moving ephemeral fields out should help. What's the recommended approach from Redwood?
[01:57] Jordan: Best practice we've been recommending is: 1) canonicalize prompt templates, 2) move per-user data to structured tool calls or metadata, 3) use a short prefix TTL for session-level personalization and longer TTL for system static prefixes. Also consider key hashing that ignores certain token ranges.
[02:14] Priya (SE): Also note, KV caches are very sensitive to encoding/normalization; we have a small patch we can push to normalize punctuation and unicode variations which gave us a +8-10% hit on a previous pilot.
[02:26] Maya: That would be great to try. Can you share the patch or a config we can apply?
[02:31] Priya (SE): Yup, i'll attach it to caching-configs-v2. Jordan will send the annotated doc with suggested TTLs.
[02:37] Jordan: Yep I'll send. On the TTL side, for Atlas traffic profile I'd suggest: prefix TTL = 24h for system templates, KV TTL = 30m for conversational reuse, and a hot-key pinning option for very high reuse prompts. But those are tunable.
[02:52] Ethan: 30 minutes sounds ok as a starting point. We're worried about staleness if we do too long.
[02:57] Samir: Tradeoff math — longer TTL increases hit rate and reduces cost but risks stale personalization. Also impacts memory footprint on the serving nodes.
[03:08] Priya (SE): Right, we can also use an LRU eviction with size cap per tenant; our runtime supports per-customer caps so memory doesn't explode.
[03:18] Maya: On the metrics, can we get separate cold/hot latencies and token counts? Right now your dashboard shows only aggregate.
[03:24] Priya (SE): Yes, i'll enable KV cache telemetry in staging to emit: kv_hits, kv_misses, prefix_hits, prefix_misses, avg_token_cost, p50/p95/p99 latency broken down by cache hit/miss.
[03:37] Jordan: Great, if we get that we can compute effective cost savings. Last week we estimated a 15% cost reduction at 50% combined hit; we can refine with your actual token distribution.
[03:48] Maya: One item — we saw occasional mismatched keys leading to cache evictions; could be due to session tokens embedding timestamps, we'll audit.
[03:57] Priya (SE): Good call, try to avoid embedding ephemeral timestamps inside the canonical prompt. Instead, pass them as tool args or separate fields.
[04:06] Ethan: Regarding benchmarks, what's the recommended test harness size? We have a 12k prompt set representing last month's traffic.
[04:13] Jordan: 12k is good. Run both cold (empty caches) and warm (preload prefixes from historical) runs. Capture hit rates over time and token-level cost. Include a run with prompt normalization applied so we can compare.
[04:26] Maya: We'll schedule nightly runs across the 1% traffic slice and share the results.
[04:31] Jordan: Perfect. Also on the engineering side, we can experiment with approximate matching thresholds for KV keys (fuzzy match) — that can boost hits for near-duplicate prompts but slightly raises complexity.
[04:42] Samir: Are there privacy or security implications with fuzzy matching?
[04:45] Priya (SE): Not really, unless you start combining user-specific fields into cache keys; we keep PII out of keys and the platform integrates with KMS for encryption at rest. It's just about token similarity.
[04:55] Priya (Atlas): Speaking of security, can you re-send the SOC2 docs? Our security team asked for updated artifacts.
[05:01] Jordan: Sure, i'll include the SOC2 and the KMS integration notes in the follow-up.
[05:06] Ethan: On deployment, we were also evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted to reduce cross-tenant noise — any recommendation?
[05:13] Jordan: For Atlas scale, Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and allows larger per-tenant cache memory caps; Hosted can be fine if you can tolerate some cold starts and smaller caps. Since you plan a production slice (10%), Dedicated pilot is reasonable but it depends on contractual / security needs.
[05:29] Priya (Atlas): We'll check cost with finance. For now we'll keep staging on hosted.
[05:33] Jordan: Sounds good. Quick recap of action items...
[05:36] Jordan: Jordan to send caching-configs-v2 with TTL recommendations and normalization patch by Friday 10/22.
[05:44] Jordan: Priya (SE) to enable KV telemetry and share dashboard link by 10/23.
[05:50] Maya: I'll run the 12k benchmark nightly and share the spreadsheet by 10/27.
[05:55] Ethan: I'll confirm the 10% production traffic slice for the pilot by 10/25.
[06:01] Priya (Atlas): Great — let's reconvene next week same time.
[06:05] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links.
[06:09] Maya: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
